title: Binary counit substitution and comparison transpose
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_i,\mathcal D_i$ for $i=1,2,3$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. Specify functors $R_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$, $L_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal C_i$ and natural transformations $u_i:1\to L_iR_i$, $e_i:R_iL_i\to1$ satisfying $L_i(e_{i,M})u_{i,L_iM}=1$ and $e_{i,R_iI}R_i(u_{i,I})=1$. Thus $R_i\dashv L_i$ is specified. Let $B:\mathcal D_1\times\mathcal D_2\to\mathcal D_3$ and $\bar B:\mathcal C_1\times\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_3$ be bifunctors, that is, functors on the product categories. Give a natural isomorphism $d_{I,J}:L_3B(R_1I,R_2J)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar B(I,J)$. Composition is right to left. Define
$$r_{I,J}=e_{3,B(R_1I,R_2J)}R_3(d_{I,J}^{-1}).$$
For $q:R_1I\to M$, $q':R_2J\to N$, put $b=L_1(q)u_{1,I}$, $b'=L_2(q')u_{2,J}$ and $q_B=B(q,q')r_{I,J}$. Then
$$q=e_{1,M}R_1(b),\quad q'=e_{2,N}R_2(b'),\quad L_3(r_{I,J})u_{3,\bar B(I,J)}=d_{I,J}^{-1},$$
$$b_B:=L_3(q_B)u_{3,\bar B(I,J)}=L_3B(q,q')d_{I,J}^{-1}=L_3B(e_{1,M},e_{2,N})d_{L_1M,L_2N}^{-1}\bar B(b,b').$$
Here $B(q,q')=B(e_{1,M},e_{2,N})B(R_1b,R_2b')$. If $b,b',e_{1,M},e_{2,N}$ are invertible, all factors in the last expression for $b_B$ are invertible, and, with
$$a_B(M,N)=d_{L_1M,L_2N}(L_3B(e_{1,M},e_{2,N}))^{-1},$$
one has
$$b_B^{-1}=\bar B(b^{-1},(b')^{-1})a_B(M,N).$$
For arbitrary maps $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$ for which all four input counits are invertible, writing $E_{M,N}=L_3B(e_{1,M},e_{2,N})$, the identities
$$E_{M',N'}^{-1}L_3B(f,g)=L_3B(R_1L_1f,R_2L_2g)E_{M,N}^{-1},$$
$$a_B(M',N')L_3B(f,g)=\bar B(L_1f,L_2g)a_B(M,N)$$
hold. The inputs and their maps are independent; the formulas also allow equal objects, repeated inputs and identity maps. No monoidal structure on the categories or faithfulness of evaluations is assumed.

proof.text:
For $(i,X,T,p)=(1,I,M,q)$ and $(2,J,N,q')$, counit naturality and the stipulated triangle give
$$e_{i,T}R_i(L_i(p)u_{i,X})=p\,e_{i,R_iX}R_i(u_{i,X})=p.$$
This is the first pair of identities; only functoriality, naturality of $e_i$, and the second displayed triangle in the hypotheses are used.

source.place: Agent-written elementary categorical elaboration, calculation 1; coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits in fix-prop-coherence

proof.text:
Set $H=B(R_1I,R_2J)$, $A=\bar B(I,J)$ and $h=d_{I,J}^{-1}:A\to L_3H$. Naturality of $u_3$ gives $L_3R_3(h)u_{3,A}=u_{3,L_3H}h$. Thus the definition of $r$ and the other stipulated triangle give
$$L_3(r_{I,J})u_{3,A}=L_3(e_{3,H})L_3R_3(h)u_{3,A}=L_3(e_{3,H})u_{3,L_3H}h=h.$$

source.place: Agent-written elementary categorical elaboration, calculation 2; coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits in fix-prop-coherence

proof.text:
Apply functoriality to $q_B=B(q,q')r_{I,J}$ and substitute step 2:
$$b_B=L_3B(q,q')L_3(r_{I,J})u_{3,A}=L_3B(q,q')d_{I,J}^{-1}.$$
In the product category composition is componentwise, so step 1 and the defining composition law of the functor $B$ give
$$B(q,q')=B(e_{1,M},e_{2,N})B(R_1(b),R_2(b')).$$

source.place: Agent-written elementary categorical elaboration, calculation 3; coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits in fix-prop-coherence

proof.text:
Naturality of $d$ at the product-category arrow $(b,b'):(I,J)\to(L_1M,L_2N)$ states
$$\bar B(b,b')d_{I,J}=d_{L_1M,L_2N}L_3B(R_1(b),R_2(b')).$$
Compose with the two inverse components of $d$ to obtain
$$L_3B(R_1(b),R_2(b'))d_{I,J}^{-1}=d_{L_1M,L_2N}^{-1}\bar B(b,b').$$
Substitute this and step 3 into $b_B$ to get precisely $b_B=E_{M,N}d_{L_1M,L_2N}^{-1}\bar B(b,b')$.

source.place: Agent-written elementary categorical elaboration, calculation 4; coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits in fix-prop-coherence

proof.text:
Under the stated invertibility hypotheses, $E_{M,N}^{-1}=L_3B(e_{1,M}^{-1},e_{2,N}^{-1})$ and $\bar B(b,b')^{-1}=\bar B(b^{-1},(b')^{-1})$: composing either proposed inverse on either side gives the image of the pair of identity arrows, hence an identity. Reverse the three factors of step 4 and cancel adjacent inverse pairs. This gives
$$b_B^{-1}=\bar B(b^{-1},(b')^{-1})d_{L_1M,L_2N}E_{M,N}^{-1}=\bar B(b^{-1},(b')^{-1})a_B(M,N).$$

source.place: Agent-written elementary categorical elaboration, calculation 5; coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits in fix-prop-coherence

proof.text:
Counit naturality says $f e_{1,M}=e_{1,M'}R_1L_1(f)$ and $g e_{2,N}=e_{2,N'}R_2L_2(g)$. Applying the functor $L_3B$ on the product category yields
$$L_3B(f,g)E_{M,N}=E_{M',N'}L_3B(R_1L_1(f),R_2L_2(g)).$$
All four counits are invertible, so both $E$ maps have the inverses described in step 5. Compose on the left by $E_{M',N'}^{-1}$ and on the right by $E_{M,N}^{-1}$ to obtain the first requested naturality equation.

source.place: Agent-written elementary categorical elaboration, calculation 6; coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits in fix-prop-coherence

proof.text:
Naturality of $d$ at $(L_1(f),L_2(g))$ gives
$$d_{L_1M',L_2N'}L_3B(R_1L_1(f),R_2L_2(g))=\bar B(L_1(f),L_2(g))d_{L_1M,L_2N}.$$
Multiply the equation of step 6 by $d_{L_1M',L_2N'}$ on the left, substitute this equality, and use $a_B=dE^{-1}$. The result is $a_B(M',N')L_3B(f,g)=\bar B(L_1(f),L_2(g))a_B(M,N)$. Each calculation treats the two coordinates independently, so equal objects, repeated inputs and identity arrows are allowed.
